```{r setup}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
em <- read.csv("gene_finder_emissions.csv")
base_cols <- c(A = "#008300", C = "#2a78d6", G = "#eda100", T = "#e34948")
th <- theme_minimal(base_size = 18) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "none")

# fraction of each base at each position of the 3-mer, for a set of
# emission groups
base_composition <- function(model_name, groups, positions = 1:3) {
  em |>
    filter(model == model_name, group %in% groups) |>
    tidyr::crossing(position = positions) |>
    mutate(base = substr(kmer, position, position)) |>
    group_by(group, position, base) |>
    summarize(prob = sum(prob), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(group = factor(group, groups))
}

logo_bars <- function(d, x) {
  ggplot(d, aes({{ x }}, prob, fill = base)) +
    geom_col(width = .85, color = "white", linewidth = .6) +
    geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(prob > .15, base, "")),
              position = position_stack(vjust = .5),
              color = "white", size = 7, fontface = "bold") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = base_cols) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0, .5, 1)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) + th
}
```

## Reading DNA three letters at a time

At each position $t$ the HMM sees the three letters centered on $t$,
and has to guess the hidden label of position $t$.

::: {.tiles}
::: {.row}
[DNA]{.lab}
[C]{.t .cd} [A]{.t .cd} [G]{.t .cd .win} [G]{.t .ss .win} [T]{.t .in .win} [A]{.t .in} [A]{.t .in} [G]{.t .in} [T]{.t .in}
:::
::: {.row}
[label]{.lab}
[coding]{.pill .cd} [donor]{.pill .ss} [intron]{.pill .in}
:::
:::

::: {.tiles}
::: {.row}
[$t$ = donor]{.lab}
[G]{.t .cd .win} [G]{.t .ss .win} [T]{.t .in .win} [sees "GGT": the G T that starts every intron]{.note}
:::
:::

Centering the three letters lets a one-letter state like the donor see
its whole signal.

To keep things simple: 100 genes on the + strand, coding sequence only,
introns cut to 200 letters, 50 genes to learn from and 50 to test on.

## The hidden states

::: {.tiles}
::: {.row}
[intergenic]{.pill .ig} [→]{.arrow} [start codon]{.pill .sc} [→]{.arrow}
[codon: 1 → 2 → 3 ↺]{.pill .cd} [→]{.arrow} [stop codon]{.pill .sc} [→]{.arrow}
[intergenic]{.pill .ig}
:::
::: {.row}
[ ]{.gap} [ ]{.gap} [ ]{.gap} [ ]{.gap} [ ]{.gap} [codon]{.pill .cd} [→]{.arrow}
[donor]{.pill .ss} [→]{.arrow} [intron ↺]{.pill .in} [→]{.arrow}
[acceptor]{.pill .ss} [→]{.arrow} [codon]{.pill .cd}
:::
:::

- Only the arrows shown are allowed. Every other entry of the
  transition matrix $A$ is 0, and stays 0 when Baum-Welch updates $A$.
- The codon states go 1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3, ... so the model reads in codons.
- An intron can interrupt a codon anywhere, so there are three copies
  of donor, intron, acceptor. Each copy remembers where in the codon
  we were, and picks up there after the intron.

## Learning the emissions: just count

On the 50 training genes we know the label of every letter, so we count
which 3-letter words appear in each state. The counts find the known
signals (each bar shows the letters at one position of the 3-letter word):

```{r counts, fig.width=12, fig.height=3.6}
groups <- c("intronic", "start2", "stop2", "donor_1", "acceptor_1")
d <- base_composition("simple", groups) |>
  mutate(group = factor(group, groups,
           c("intron (typical)", "start codon", "stop codon", "donor", "acceptor")),
         position = factor(position, 1:3, c("t-1", "t", "t+1")))
logo_bars(d, position) + facet_wrap(~group, nrow = 1)
```

We keep these counts fixed, and use Baum-Welch on the test genes only to
learn how often the states switch, the transition matrix $A$.

## Each letter is seen three times

```{=html}
<div class="tiles">
<div class="row"><span class="lab">DNA</span>
<span class="t ig">A</span><span class="t ig">C</span><span class="t cd win">G</span><span class="t ig">T</span><span class="t ig">A</span></div>
<div class="row"><span class="lab">at t-1</span>
<span class="t cd">A</span><span class="t cd">C</span><span class="t cd">G</span></div>
<div class="row"><span class="lab">at t</span><span class="gap"></span>
<span class="t cd">C</span><span class="t cd">G</span><span class="t cd">T</span></div>
<div class="row"><span class="lab">at t+1</span><span class="gap"></span><span class="gap"></span>
<span class="t cd">G</span><span class="t cd">T</span><span class="t cd">A</span></div>
</div>
```

The HMM treats each 3-letter word as new evidence, so it is three times
too sure of itself, and jumps between states too easily. Fix: shrink
the emission probabilities, $B^w$ with $w < 1$.

```{r weight, fig.width=12, fig.height=3}
acc <- data.frame(
  w = rep(c("1", "1/2", "1/3"), 2),
  what = rep(c("letters labeled correctly", "codon position correct"), each = 3),
  pct = c(62, 74, 70, 73, 94, 98))
acc$w <- factor(acc$w, c("1", "1/2", "1/3"))
acc$what <- factor(acc$what, unique(acc$what))
ggplot(acc, aes(w, pct)) +
  geom_col(width = .6, fill = "#2a78d6") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(pct, "%")), vjust = -.4, size = 6) +
  facet_wrap(~what) + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 108), breaks = NULL) +
  labs(x = "w", y = NULL) + th
```

## Longer splice sites: more states

Short exons were skipped: two rare jumps (into and out of the intron)
cost more than a short exon's evidence. Fix: let the donor and acceptor
each be a chain of states, 4 letters and 6 letters long. The counted
letters along each chain spell out the known splice signals:

```{r chains, fig.width=12, fig.height=3}
donor <- paste0("donor_", 1:4)
acceptor <- paste0("acceptor_", 1:6)
d <- base_composition("advanced", c(donor, acceptor), positions = 2) |>
  mutate(site = ifelse(grepl("donor", group), "start of intron (donor)",
                       "end of intron (acceptor)"),
         site = factor(site, c("start of intron (donor)", "end of intron (acceptor)")))
logo_bars(d, group) + facet_wrap(~site, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x) sub(".*_", "", x))
```

```{r models, fig.width=12, fig.height=2.4}
res <- data.frame(
  model = rep(c("simple (19 states)", "longer splice sites (43 states)"), 2),
  what = rep(c("letters labeled correctly", "coding letters found"), each = 2),
  pct = c(74, 78, 65, 78))
res$model <- factor(res$model, unique(res$model))
res$what <- factor(res$what, unique(res$what))
ggplot(res, aes(pct, model, fill = model)) +
  geom_col(width = .6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(pct, "%")), hjust = -.15, size = 6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#8a8984", "#2a78d6")) +
  facet_wrap(~what) + scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), breaks = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) + th
```
